title: Retention enforcement reporting
description:
Emit a structured report after each GC run showing what was deleted, when, and why — so operators have proof that retention policies are being enforced and can audit storage reclamation.

Why this issue exists:
The GC runs on a cron schedule and currently logs a single summary line. Operators subject to retention obligations (legal hold, GDPR deletion requests, data lifecycle policies) need a durable, structured record of what was actually deleted. 'Trust me, the GC ran' is not sufficient for compliance.

Scope:
- After each GC run, write a structured retention report to a configurable path (default: /var/log/usenet-ipfs/gc-reports/YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ.json)
- Report fields: run_id (UUID), started_at, completed_at, policy (the GC policy that ran), groups_scanned, articles_evaluated, articles_deleted, bytes_reclaimed, errors (list of CIDs that failed to unpin with reason)
- Also emit a single structured log event at INFO summarizing the run: event=gc_complete with the same top-level counts
- Expose Prometheus counters: gc_runs_total, gc_articles_deleted_total, gc_bytes_reclaimed_total
- Report files are never deleted by the daemon — retention of the reports themselves is the operator's responsibility
- Add GET /admin/gc/last-run to the admin endpoint returning the most recent report as JSON

Acceptance criteria:
- After a GC run that deletes articles, a report file exists at the configured path with valid JSON
- The report lists each deleted article's CID and the policy rule that matched
- GET /admin/gc/last-run returns the same data as the most recent report file
- gc_articles_deleted_total in /metrics increments by the correct count after a GC run
- A GC run that deletes nothing still writes a report (with articles_deleted: 0)
